project.title: Stock Price Movement Predictor
project.objective: Predict the next trading day's direction (UP = 1, DOWN = 0) of the NIFTY 50 index from daily OHLCV data, without temporal leakage.

target.code:
next_close = df["Close"].shift(-1)
df["Target"] = np.where(next_close.isna(), np.nan,
                        (next_close > df["Close"]).astype(float))
target.positiveLabel: UP (1): the next session closes higher
target.negativeLabel: DOWN (0): the next session closes lower or unchanged

leakageChecks.name: Dates sorted chronologically
leakageChecks.detail: 2879 sessions from 2015-01-02 to 2026-09-10 are strictly increasing.

leakageChecks.name: Target equals next-day movement
leakageChecks.detail: Independent recomputation of 1[Close(t+1) > Close(t)] matches all 2878 labels; the final row's label is undefined (NaN).

leakageChecks.name: Final unlabeled row excluded
leakageChecks.detail: 2026-09-10 has no next close and is absent from the modeling data.

leakageChecks.name: No look-ahead constructs in feature code
leakageChecks.detail: Syntax-tree scan of features.py and baselines.py found no negative shift, centred window, backward fill or interpolation; 1 shift(periods) call(s) take a variable lag, which trailing_return() restricts to positive values and the truncation test verifies numerically.

leakageChecks.name: Features unchanged when the future is removed
leakageChecks.detail: All 14 features recomputed on 40 truncated histories; largest absolute difference = 0.0e+00.

leakageChecks.name: Target and next-day columns excluded from features
leakageChecks.detail: Neither feature set contains Target, Next_Close, Next_Date or the Persistence helper columns.

leakageChecks.name: No NaN or infinite values in model inputs
leakageChecks.detail: 2233 train and 558 test rows x 14 features are all finite.

leakageChecks.name: Train period ends before test period
Every training label resolved before the test window
leakageChecks.detail: Latest Close(t+1) used by a training label is from 2024-06-04; 1 embargo row(s) purged.

leakageChecks.name: Chronological split, no shuffling
leakageChecks.detail: Train + embargo + test reproduce the original date order exactly; no random split is used.

leakageChecks.name: Scaler fitted on training rows only (Raw OHLCV)
leakageChecks.detail: StandardScaler saw 2233 rows (= training rows) and its Close mean 12,876.7 equals the training mean, not the train+test mean 15,197.5.

leakageChecks.name: Scaler fitted on training rows only (Engineered Features)
leakageChecks.detail: StandardScaler saw 2233 rows (= training rows) and its Close mean 12,876.7 equals the training mean, not the train+test mean 15,197.5.

leakageChecks.name: Hyper-parameter search never sees the test set
leakageChecks.detail: All 5 TimeSeriesSplit folds (gap = 1) index only the 2233 training rows, and each validation block starts after its fitting block ends.

leakageChecks.name: Majority class taken from training labels
leakageChecks.detail: Training UP share 53.92% -> predict UP. (The test-set majority, UP, was not used.)

leakageChecks.name: Persistence uses only information up to day t
leakageChecks.detail: Persistence(t) = 1[Close(t) > Close(t-1)] recomputed independently for every test day; it matches the realised next-day label on 54.1% of days (a rule that could see tomorrow would match 100%).

leakageChecks.name: All four approaches scored on the same test days
leakageChecks.detail: Persistence, Majority Class, Raw OHLCV, Engineered Features each predict the same 558 sessions (2024-06-05 to 2026-09-09).

leakageChecks.name: Comparison table reproduces from saved predictions
leakageChecks.detail: Accuracy in four_way_comparison.csv equals the accuracy recomputed from test_predictions.csv for all 4 approaches.

leakageChecks.name: Prediction plot drawn from actual test predictions
leakageChecks.detail: The 558 predictions plotted equal a fresh pipeline.predict() on the test features, in chronological order.

cv.method: TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=5, gap=1) inside the training window; C grid [0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0]; selection metric: accuracy

nextSession.note: Output of the evaluated engineered model for the first session after the data ends. Research output only: not a trading signal or investment advice.

findings.question: Did the raw model beat Persistence?
findings.answer: Raw OHLCV accuracy 50.36% vs Persistence 54.12% (-3.76 pp).

findings.question: Did the raw model beat Majority Class?
findings.answer: Raw OHLCV accuracy 50.36% vs Majority 50.36% (+0.00 pp). The raw model predicted UP on 100.0% of test days.

findings.question: Did the engineered model beat the raw model?
findings.answer: Engineered 50.36% vs Raw 50.36% (+0.00 pp); exact McNemar p = 1.000 on 0 discordant days.

findings.question: Did the engineered model beat both naive baselines?
findings.answer: vs Persistence -3.76 pp; vs Majority +0.00 pp.

findings.question: By how much?
findings.answer: Against the stronger baseline (Persistence) the engineered model differs by -3.76 pp. Its 95% Wilson interval for accuracy is 46.2% to 54.5%.

findings.question: Is the improvement practically meaningful or only marginal?
findings.answer: The difference to Persistence is -3.76 pp with exact McNemar p = 0.229. The project's pre-set bar for 'meaningful' is at least 2 pp AND p < 0.05; this bar is not met.

findings.question: How does class imbalance affect interpretation?
findings.answer: UP days are 53.9% of training labels and 50.4% of test labels, so always predicting 'UP' already scores 50.36%. Accuracy must be read relative to that floor; balanced accuracy (Engineered 50.00%, Raw 50.00%) removes the advantage of favouring the majority class.

findings.question: Are there signs that the model is close to naive performance?
findings.answer: The engineered model is +0.00 pp from the Majority baseline, predicts UP on 100.0% of days and has ROC-AUC 0.506 (0.5 = no ranking skill).

limitations: Financial markets are noisy and non-stationary; next-day direction is close to a coin flip and small accuracy differences can arise by chance.
Relationships learned from 2015-2024 can weaken or reverse in a new regime (policy shocks, pandemics, changes in market microstructure).
Technical indicators summarise past prices; they carry no guarantee of predictive power.

Raw price levels (Open, High, Low, Close, SMA_20, EMA_20) and MACD in index points are non-stationary: the test period trades at levels partly outside the training range, which a linear model extrapolates poorly.
One index over one period does not establish that the approach generalises to other assets or markets.
Classification accuracy is not trading profitability: transaction costs, slippage, taxes and position sizing are not modelled, and no trading strategy was evaluated.
The test window is a single chronological hold-out; results on other windows could differ.
Yahoo Finance data can be revised, and a few sessions lack reported volume; the committed snapshot and its checksum pin the data used here.
